name: US (general)
authority: US EPA and The Recycling Partnership

sources.label: EPA: How do I recycle common recyclables
The Recycling Partnership: What can I recycle

bins.name: Recycling
bins.accepts: Curbside cart: bottles, cans, paper, cardboard

bins.name: Compost
bins.accepts: Food and yard waste, where offered

bins.name: Drop-off
bins.accepts: Store take-back or hazardous waste site

prep: Caps and labels can stay on
plastic_bottle.why: Plastic bottles are among the most commonly recycled items.

prep: Check that your program takes this plastic
plastic_container.why: Many programs accept rigid containers; items with food on them can't be recycled.

prep: Check that your program takes cups
plastic_cup.why: Acceptance depends on the local program.

plastic_lid_cap.why: Bottles and caps are on EPA's common recyclables list.

prep: Return clean, dry bags to a store drop-off
plastic_bag_film.why: Plastic bags are recyclable, but not in your household recycling bin.

snack_wrapper.why: Wraps and film can't go in a curbside recycling bin.

foam.why: Very few localities accept Styrofoam in curbside recycling.

plastic_utensil_straw.why: EPA says plastic utensils can't be recycled. Some cities, like NYC, do accept them.

paper.why: Paper, mail and newspapers are recyclable when clean and dry.

paper_bag.why: Paper must be empty, clean and dry to be recycled.

cardboard.why: Cardboard is one of the most commonly recycled items.

prep: Very greasy? Compost if you can
pizza_box.why: EPA says pizza boxes can be recycled, even with some grease.

soiled_paper.why: Food-soiled paper never goes in recycling but may be compostable.

prep: Check your local list: some programs take them
paper_cup.why: Coated paper cups are not on EPA's common recyclables list.

carton.why: Carton acceptance depends on the local program.

metal_can.why: Soda and soup cans are accepted almost everywhere.

prep: Only if your local program lists foil
aluminum_foil.why: EPA says foil can be recycled; programs differ.

prep: Empty: some programs take it with metal
aerosol_can.why: Aerosol cans that aren't empty must never go in recycling.

prep: Larger scrap metal: a scrap metal recycler
metal_lid_scrap.why: Curbside programs usually take metal cans, not loose small metal.

glass_bottle_jar.why: Glass jars are on EPA's most-common list; a few programs exclude glass.

drinking_glass_ceramic.why: Broken glass should not go in the recycling bin.

food_scraps.why: Food can't be recycled, but it can be composted.

yard_waste.why: Lawn materials can't be recycled, but they can be composted.

prep: Retail drop-off or hazardous waste event
battery.why: Batteries should not go in household garbage or recycling bins.

prep: Collection site, maker or retailer take-back
Donate or use a retail take-back
textile.why: Textiles can't go in a curbside recycling bin.

shoes.why: Gently worn shoes can be donated to many charities.

cigarette_butt.why: Not on any common recyclables list.

blister_pack.why: Mixed plastic and foil packaging is not on common recyclables lists.

rope_string.why: Hoses and similar tanglers are on EPA's never-recycle list.

squeezable_tube.why: Not on EPA's common recyclables list.

mask_gloves.why: Not on EPA's common recyclables list.
